description: Lists the alarms of a WinCC Unified HMI as {hmi, kind, alarms:[{kind, name, alarmClass, priority, triggerTag, triggerBit, triggerBitAddress, triggerMode, condition, conditionValue, triggerAddress, eventText}], total, nextCursor, inventoryGaps}. Discrete alarms come first, then analog ones; a discrete alarm fills triggerBit, triggerBitAddress and triggerMode, an analog one fills condition, conditionValue and triggerAddress, and the fields of the other kind are null. eventText is {culture name: plain text or null} for every active project language: TIA stores the text as rich text and the serve answers a body that holds one paragraph of text only as that plain text (an item without text is an empty string, a language without an item null); any other markup comes back unchanged as raw rich text, which cannot be written back. conditionValue is a JSON number, except a whole value held by an integer-backed trigger tag (LInt, ULInt, LWord, ...) whose magnitude is greater than 2^53: that is a decimal string, up to 18446744073709551615 (TIA stores the value as a double, so only an alarm that already existed could hold one: unverified that TIA reports it). A Real or LReal value is always a number, even when whole and large (1e20), so it can be passed back as input. `kind` limits the list to discrete or analog alarms and is echoed back. Use it before creating, updating or deleting an alarm. For a large HMI read it in pages: pass limit (1-1000), then pass the nextCursor of each page as cursor until nextCursor is null; total is the number of alarms of the whole list. Without limit and cursor the whole list is returned with nextCursor null. A cursor of a list that changed is 409 cursor_stale (restart without cursor), one that is not a nextCursor is 400 invalid_cursor. `inventoryGaps` [{kind, subject, reason}] lists every value or object the serve could not read while building the answer (empty when all reads succeeded): the unreadable value is null and one gap names it, so a null next to a gap means unreadable, while a value the object does not offer is null without a gap. Needs an open project and a WinCC Unified HMI (hmi = its name from tia_hmis, matched ignoring case): a classic WinCC HMI is refused with 409 hmi_not_unified, an unknown HMI is 404 not_found and two HMIs with the same name are 409 ambiguous_name. Maps to GET /hmi/{hmi}/alarms?kind=&limit=&cursor= (all optional). Read-only (class R).

cursor.description: the nextCursor of the previous page, passed back exactly as received; it is opaque, so never invent, build or edit one (omit it for the first page, and omit both limit and cursor for the whole list)

hmi.description: HMI name, as listed by tia_hmis (a WinCC Unified HMI)

kind.description: only discrete or only analog alarms; omit for both

limit.description: page size, an integer from 1 to 1000; pass it to read the list in pages (omit both limit and cursor for the whole list)

name: tia_hmi_alarms
title: TIA — HMI Unified alarms
